title: Jülich Supercomputing Centre Benchmark Evaluates Quantum Error Correction Primitives Across Quantinuum, IBM, and IQM Hardware - Quantum Computing Report
gist: A Jülich Supercomputing Centre benchmark of QEC primitives (mid-circuit measurement, reset, feed-forward, spectator idling) across ten commercial QPUs from Quantinuum, IBM and IQM finds Quantinuum’s trapped-ion machines strongest, with IBM’s mid-circuit measurement error still about 10x its two-qubit gate error.

insights.claim: Researchers at Jülich Supercomputing Centre benchmarked QEC primitives (mid-circuit measurement, qubit reset, dynamic feed-forward control and spectator idling) across ten commercial QPUs from Quantinuum, IBM and IQM.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An independent, cross-vendor comparison on QEC building blocks is rare; useful for judging who is closest to fault tolerance.

insights.claim: The study introduces a low-sampling algorithmic benchmark based on Linear-Ramp QAOA that embeds the interaction and check structures of surface codes, triangular color codes and bivariate-bicycle qLDPC codes, and measures effective depolarizing error rates (λeff) over repeated syndrome-extraction rounds.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A cheap proxy metric for QEC readiness could become a standard way to compare hardware without full logical-qubit experiments.

insights.claim: The low-shot LR-QAOA metric correlated strongly (Spearman ρs of 0.83 to 0.88) with actual logical-error survival probabilities in an 11-patch distance-3 surface-code memory experiment on ibm_phoenix.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Validation against real logical memory runs supports the benchmark as a usable proxy.

insights.claim: Quantinuum’s trapped-ion systems showed the strongest overall QEC-primitive performance, with mid-circuit measurement error comparable to two-qubit gate error (λeff about 0.22% to 0.49%) and scale up to distance-11 color codes (91 data qubits) and distance-9 surface codes (81 data qubits).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Supports Quantinuum’s lead on error-correction-relevant fidelity and connectivity versus superconducting peers.
insights.quote: Quantinuum’s trapped-ion systems demonstrated the strongest overall performance across the tested QEC primitives

insights.claim: Quantinuum maintained algorithmic signal (r = 0.733) on a 91-data-qubit triangular color code requiring 45 mid-circuit measurements per layer across 98 physical qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Evidence of working large-width, deep QEC circuits on trapped-ion hardware.

insights.claim: On IBM’s Heron processors (e.g. ibm_boston) mid-circuit measurement shows generational improvement but its error rate remains roughly 10x that of baseline two-qubit gates (λeff about 1.1% to 3.2%), and tested surface codes reached only distance 5 (25 data qubits).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Mid-circuit measurement is an identified bottleneck for IBM’s QEC roadmap; track improvements in later Heron/successor generations.

insights.claim: On IQM’s Emerald and Garnet devices, algorithmic signal decayed faster beyond 2-data-qubit chains because of conditional-control and routing constraints, so only 1D MCM chains and minimal triplet configurations were tested.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IQM’s current hardware appears limited for dynamic-circuit QEC experiments relative to Quantinuum and IBM.
